description: The collections the Clay runtime defines for shells. A collection is a token def named by `nsid#def`, with its row key and row value as sibling defs of this file.

roots.description: The collection a shell micro reads its roots from (`org.example.clay.shell#roots`). A micro registers one row, keyed by its own micro id (`rootKey`), that holds the root presentation it offers (`root`); the shell mounts each one it finds.

rootKey.description: The key of a `roots` row: the id of the micro that registered it.

title.description: What the shell calls the root.

content.description: A Clay link: a CBOR tag wrapping an index into the row's links, naming the presentation the root mounts. Rows are CBOR, not atproto data, and the link's JSON spelling `{"$link": index}` collides with the reserved `$link` of the atproto data model (a CID), so this def documents the shape and no Lexicon codec admits a link.
